FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted the Pulleys and Belts Sectional Engineering Division Council. by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by Committee had been approved by the Light Mechanical

In the manufacture or repair of a conveyor belt, it is necessary to join the ends of a length of belting at site as it may not be possible to do this in the workshop for various reasons, for example: a) the need to fit the belting accurately to the conveyor or structure on site, b) the belting has to be threaded on to the structure prior to jointing, and c) when effecting repairs to a belt by inserting a new section of belting it may not be economic or safe to remove the belt from the structure. On-site non-mechanical jointing of plied textile reinforced rubber conveyor vulcanizing will be covered in Part 2 of this standard which is under preparation. In the preparation of this standard, considerable Code of practice for on-site non-mechanical conveyor belting'. assistance jointing belting by cold

has been derived from BS 6593 : 1985 of plied textile and steel reinforced

1 GENERAL

3.5 Plied textile reinforced rubber conveyor belting - Fire resistant grade as per IS 1891 ( Part 5 ) : 1993. 4 SAFETY GUIDANCE 4.1 General The instructions and procedures given under 4.2 to 4.5 should be followed at all times during the preparation and manufacture of non-mechanical joints in conveyor belting. 4.2 Access and Power Supplies Proper means of access should be provided. If scaffolding is needed, it should be erected according to current safety practice and proper access provided. Proper lighting arrangement for working area should be made. Before starting the job, plant should be electrically isolated and where a permit to work is required, this should be obtained from the site supervisor and retained on the job. All portable equipment power supplies and plug should be compatible with the site supplies. 4.3 Equipment Equipment used in the vulcanizing of conveyor belting is subject to statutory requirement, for example, Health and Safety Acts, Mining Acts and other Regulations prevailing in the country. The maximum operating width of the equipment shall be more than the width of the belt to be vulcanized. 4.4 Jointing Materials Good house-keeping should be maintained. Following precautions should be taken during handling of jointing materials, used in the preparation of vulcanized joints:

6 GENERAL

6.1 Training The quality of joint depends upon the quality of the equipment used and skill of the operator. Adequate skill will only be achieved by proper training and on the job experience. 6.1.1 All operators should have training both in the workshop and followed by a period of strict on supervision before they are regarded qualified to carry out jointing work on 6.1.2 Training records should readily available for inspection. 6.2 Maintenance of Equipment The equipment used in making joints in belting should be regularly maintained. Cutting devices should be kept sharp and any templates used should be regularly checked for dimensional accuracy. Mechanical, electrical, hydraulic and pneumatic equipment should be regularly checked for correct operation and repaired, if It is most important that temperanecessary. ture indicators, pressure gauges and test equipment are accurately and regularly calibrated. The earthing of electrical equipment, the security of guards on presses and soundness of hydraulic and pneumatic hose should be ensured. 2 sufficient on site, the job as being site. and

IS 14206 ( Part 1 ) : 1995 7 TOOLS AND EQUIPMENT 7.1 General All tools, equipment and jointing material should, as far as possible, comply with the recomrelevant Indian Standards, or as mended by the belt manufacturer/vulcanizing manufacturer. 7.2 Press It is the most important equipment required for belt jointing. Press should be capable of exerting the required pressure and of maintaining a controlled temperature to suit the range of belt constructions to be joined. Press platens should be suitably designed so that in conjunction with the pressure beams, the load is uniform across the surface of the belting. The press should be regularly checked with straightedge to ensure platen flatness and also for even temperature distribution. The platens should be at least 100 mm wider than the belt width to be jointed. When the joint can be covered in a single heat, the overlap of good belt should be 50 mm on each side of the joint. When the ,joint is required to be vulcanized by multiple heat, a minimum of 50 mm overlap on cured side should be given in each heat. It is advisable to use side iron bar 0,4 mm thinner than the belt thickness on each side of the platen to prevent spreading of joint under pressure. Records should be kept of the checks for flatness and temperature distribution of the Spare thermometers shouId be carried platens. to replace defective/damaged thermometer, if any, on site. It is advisable to use press with cooled ends and platens that can be cooled with cold water to avoid delay in vulcanizing the joint. 7.3 Ancillary Equipment Following use: equipment should be available for useful to prevent overcutting damaging other plies; and

iii) 50 mm wide hand-roller for rolling down the unvulcanized joint; iv) narrow serrated stitch wheel for rolling down along ply ends; v) pincers for stripping off covers and plies; vi) scissors for cutting gum; vii) `V'-knives for trimming raw cover filler strip; viii) pricker for releasing any trapped air; ix) side bars and carpenter's clamps; and x) wooden planket or wooden platform. 8 JOINTING MATERIALS 8.1 Jointing material should be obtained from a reputed supplier and should be suitably matched to the specification of the belt to be joined. Care should be taken to ensure that shelf lives are not exceeded. Following material are required for jointing:

taken to ensure that the correct pressure is applied over the jointing area. Any low pressure at any thin section will lead to weak joint. 9.6 Jointing Used to New Belt When jointing a new belting to used one, the precautions outlined in 9.2 to 9.5 should be considered. Particular attention should be given to ( a ) the difference in thickness of the used belting with new belting, which should not exceed 1.5 mm, and ( b ) compatibility in respect of belt type and strength. It is preferable that only belts with same number of plies are jointed together. If belts having different number of plies are jointed, the difference in number of plies should not :xceed by o3e. Belts with different strength may be jointed. LO RIGGING THE BELT IN PREPARATION

9.1 General While jointing a belt, it may be ( a ) New belt with new belt, ( b ) New belt with used belt or, ( c ) used belt with used belt provided the used belts are in reasonably good conditions. In jointing the used ( b) or ( c ) the precautions given under 9.2 to 9.5 should be considered IO avoid defective or weak jointing. 9.2 Wet Belt Belts running in wet conditions absorb water. If this is allowed to remain in the belt during rejointing, pockets of vapour will be created within the joint area, reducing the overall strength of the joint during the running of the belt. These pockets propagate to produce larger area where adhesion is nil. Before attempting to joint such belts the prepared ends of the belts should be thoroughly dried either by natural means or by the use of electrica heaters. If it is impracticable to remove the belt from the conveyor because of its size and design it is recommended that a temporary shelter should be erected for drying the prepared ends and subsequently for jointing. 9.3 Oily and Greasy Conveyor Belt With some belt constructions free oil or grease present in it will be absorbed in the belting materials thus making these belts very difficult to rejoint. Carbon tetrachloride may be used for cleaning the oily and greasy belt. 9.4 The Effect of Chemicals on Jointing Used Belt Many chemicals used in process industries are absorbed into belt material. These cannot be easily removed or detected. Such chemicals Therefore, careful cause problem in belt joint. consideration should be given when jointing belts that have carried chemicals like calcium chloride, calcium sulphate, sulphur dioxide, anti-foaming oils, potash. In all such cases, advice from belt manufacturer should be sought. 9.5 Physical Condition of Used Belt Many used belts vary in thickness in their This can be due to uneven loadcross-section. When ing, uneven wear and misalignment. attempting to joint such belts, care should be 4

10.1 Positioning At first the vulcanizing team should be certain that there is sufficient belting on tbe conveyor to complete the vulcanized joint. A suitable location for splice should be chosen and the belting should be tensioned around the conveyor in all but the joint area. A typical conveyor arrangement is shown in Fig. 1. In selecting the most suitable location for splice, consideration for the following points should be given:

a) Space should be available

for suitable working table to be erected in the joint area on which to prepare the ends of the belt.

b) The location

should offer ease of operation for handling and positioning of a heavy press.

Suitable anchorage points should be available for belt clamps and tensioning equipment. A reasonable working environment be provided. should

Protection of working area from adverse weather conditions and adequate lighting arrangements should be provided wherSteps should be taken ever necessary. to exclude dust and dirt from the jointing area. The joint should at all times be kept dry.

10.2 Tensioning 10.2.1 Before tensioning, any fixed take-up devices should be secured at their minimum positions and any gravity take-up devices should be in their desired final position. On inclined conveyor belt, tensioning is easier at the lower end of the conveyor. 10.2.3 The

belt should be tensioned in the direction of normal travel.

by pulling

10.2.4 When the conditions in 10.2.1 to 10.2.3 have been met satisfactorily, belt should be tensioned to remove all belt sag between carrying and return idlers.
11 BELT JOINTING 11.1 Design of Splice and Joint Conditions 11.1.1 Stepped Bias Joint

10.2.2 Belt tensioning should be done by the use of belt clamps. These should be fixed to the belt at a suitable distance from each end to allow the vulcanized joint to be completed in the area between them after the belt has been tightened by drawing them together using suitable tensioning devices.

It is the most common joint construction and should be followed for all synthetic plied belt jointing. Figure 2 shows a typical stepped bias joint. Table 1 gives the minimum recommended step length and overall joint length multiply belting respectively.

iii) Mark off a base line over the centre line perpendicular to it and at a distance of total splice length + 50 mm from ends. The base line and centre line must be used for all future measurement. Draw another line parallel to the base Strip off line 25 mm away from it. the cover between these two lines and with a marking pencil, remark the splice line on the outer ply and remove another 25 mm wide strip of cover rubber outward of the splice line. It is to be ensured that the splice is visible when the two strip of cover rubber has been removed. iv) Cut through the first ply along the splice line using a single ply knife. Great care should be taken to-ensure that the second ply is untouched. Remove the tist ply and face cover in v) strips of 25 mm to 40 mm outward to splice line. vi) Mark off bias plus step length along belt edge from base line and draw step line. Cut the second ply as given in ( iv ) and remove the second ply in strips of 25 mm to 40 mm. 10

vii) Mark the other steps from base line and prepare in the same way. viii) Cut through the last ply and back cover at the end of the splice to make the last step 12 mm longer than the normal step length. ix) Remove back cover for a strip of 38 mm from last of the splice. x) Repeat the stripping down operations for the reverse side of the belt on the other end commending by marking the bias length along the belt edge from the base line opposite to leading end. 11.3 Preparation of Belt Ends for Chevron Splice 0 Cut the two ends square. ii) Mark off the centre lines on face cover of the leading end and back cover of trail end. iii) Draw a base line on centre line and perpendicular to it on both ends at a distance of splice length + 50 mm from outer ends. The centre line and base lines should be used for all future measurements.

IS 14206 ( Part 1) : 1995 iv) Mark off a point on the centre line of the leading end at a distance of O-5 W. Joint this point with the two edge points of the base line. Draw two lines parallel to these two lines at a distance of 25 mm towards the outward end. v) Cut the face cover between these lines and strip off the cover rubber. Now mark these two lines with a coloured pencil. vi) Strip off another 25 mm wide strip of cover rubber towards the outward end. vii) Cut the first ply along the splice line with a single ply cutter knife. Strip off the first ply and the face cover in outward direction in strip of 25 mm to 40 mm. viii) Mark the centre line again and draw a point on centre line at a distance of O-SW+step length from base line. Draw two point on both edges at a distance of splice line and join them with previous point. Cut the second ply and strip off as before. ix) Repeat the operation till the last ply. x) Cut the last ply along with back cover at a length of bias length + 25 mm. xi) Remove 38 mm strip of back cover from the last end. xii) Repeat the above operations on the trail end starting from the back cover and the bias in opposite direction. 12 CLEANING OF SPLICE AREA to ensure satisfactory bonding. the whole splice area properly. 13 JOINTING OF DIAGONAL CHEVRON SPLICE AND Clean

0 Point the steps at each end of the belt
with two coats of solution, ensuring that each coat is properly dried before proceeding with the next operation.

12.1 Cleaning of Splice Area for Synthetic Belting for Diagonal Splice 0 Using coarse emery cloth and wire brush, clean the surface of the ply steps without damaging the fabric and without disturbing the reddish coloured dip coating of the fabric. One should remember that this coating is responsible for bonding with rubber. Any damage or removal of dip coating will lead to poor bonding and hence premature splice joint failure. to ii) Buff the rubber cover adjustment splice to ensure satisfactory bonding. Clean the whole splice area properly. 12.2 Cleaning of Splice Area for Cotton and Cotton/Nylon Belting for Chevron Splice i) Using a hand grinder and wire brush, clean the surface of the ply steps without damaging the fabric. ii) Buff the rubber cover adjacent to splice

ii) Apply one layer of O-5 mm ( two where 1 mm skin is called for ) calendered carcass skin gum to the steps of the leading end of the belt and roll down well. In case of jump type splice on 2-ply belt several layers of skim gum should be used to build up the centre part of the splice as shown in Fig. 3. iii) Lay out the belt end prepared with skin gum and fit the other end to it. When matching the two ends together, it is advisable to leave the protective backing supplied with the carcass skin gum in place so that the surfaces do not adhere. Make sure that the splice is properly aligned and that the fabric steps do not overlap at any point. It is equally important not to leave gaps between steps. It is also important to check that there is no twist in the belt. iv) When the splice is perfectly matched turn back one half and remove the backing and then match and roll down the splice. v) Dig in and trim off the overlapping end of last ply on the face and back to make a close fitting joint. vi) Apply solution to edges of rubber along channel in covers. Insert strip of O-5 mm carcass skin gum. APPLY a further coat of solution and then fill in with cover splicing gum of appropriate gauge. prick the whole vii) Roll and thoroughly splice area. viii) Remove working surface from conveyor into and place vulcanizing press position. 14 VULCANIZATION i) It may be necessary due to the length of the splice to cure the splice in more than one charge. Make sure on the first and last charge that the ends of the splice are atleast 50 mm inside the platens of the vulcanizer and that an adequate overlap of 50 mm exist between subsequent charges. 11

IS 14206 ( Part 1 ) : 1995 ii) Place side irons 0*4mm less in thickness than that of the belt along the edges of the belt and press them up against belt just sufficient to make contact with the belt by means of a joiner's clamp and tighten these clamps. iii) Position the top section of the press and set to required pressure and temperature as given below. iv) After curing the splice, remove the vulcanizing press, trimmed off excess spew and examine. 14.1 Vulcanizing Pressure The vulcanizer should be set according to the maker's instructions and the type of machine, so as to give a minimum curing pressure between press platen and belt surface of 7 kg/cm2. 14.2 Vulcanizing Temperature

15 INSPECTION

OF JOINT

The joint area should be thorougly inspected. Any sign of blistering or lack of adhesion should be looked for particularly if the belt has been wet. Any such area should be opened and rejoined by vulcanization. There should be no significant change in width or thickness of the belting at the joint portion. Any discolouration of the material at the joint should be regarded with suspicion as this may indicate decomposition due to over heating. 16 TESTING If possible,
joint to

OF JOINT

the belt should be flexed at the that there are no weak areas due to lack of adhesion. In most cases, determining the hardness of the rubber at the vulcanized joint and comparing it with the hardness of parent belting may give an indication of the degree of cure of the joint. A hand held shore A durometer or IRHD meter would be suitable instrument to carry out such test.
ensure

mm

I7 LEAVING SITE
establishing that the joint is sound and neatly made, all equipment should be cleaned and removed. All waste material should be removed and the working area and its surroundings should also be cleaned. Finally the belt should be run by the client in presence of the contractor aad then reinspected ( see 15 ) to ensure that the joint is satisfactory. Documentation including sign-off of any permit to work should be completed and the client advised that the work has been completed. After

Enquiries relating to copyright be addressed to the Director ( Publications ), BIS. Revision of Indian Standards Amendments are issued to standards as the need arises on the basis of comments. Standards are also reviewed periodically; a standard along with amendments is reaffirmed when such review indicates that no changes are needed; if the review indicates that changes are needed, it is taken up for revision. Users of Indian Standards should ascertain that they are in possession of the latest amendments or edition by referring to the latest issue of `BIS Handbook' and SStandards Monthly Addition'.
